applicable_failures: Scan prefiltered by file type: the case statement only reads .docx, .xlsx, .eml, .txt and .md and does `exit 0` for every other extension, so PDFs, .doc and other formats were never searched, yet the agent claims to have covered all 9,288 files.

Narrow regex: the pattern requires 'cascade' within 80 characters of 'retail' or 'holdings', or the token 'CRH'. Bare 'Cascade' mentions, 'Cascade Retail' split across XML tags (the script only breaks lines at '<'), and other name variants would be missed.
Coverage never confirmed: the final check ran `cut -d/ -f3` on hit paths only. It did not list all matter folders or count files scanned by type, so the 'every matter covered' claim is unsupported.
critique.concerns: The agent claims all 9,288 files were scanned and that every matter was confirmed covered. The script silently skips unsupported extensions. The regex is also tight, and splitting only on '<' can break names that span XML runs. Hits are mostly .eml files, so formal documents may be missed. Zero-hit matters were never checked against the matter list.
critique.recommendation: Count files by extension under documents/matters and identify any skipped types. Extract text from those types too, or run a plain-text grep over them. Re-run with looser variants such as 'Cascade' alone, 'Cascade Retail', and 'CRH', and write each pattern's full hit list to a file. Compare the matter folder list with the matters scanned. Then open the hit matters' own documents.
